questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major iron ore belt in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haryana - Rajasthan Belt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iron ore belt in India:-**

 
 
• The iron ore belt in India refers to the region that contains high-quality iron ore deposits.
 
• It is located in the central and southern parts of the country.
 
• The iron ore belt stretches from the state of Odisha in the east to Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and Andhra Pradesh in the central and southern regions.
 
 
 
• **Haryana - Rajasthan Belt is not an iron ore belt. **(Hence option 2 is correct)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Maharashtra-Goa belt:-**

 
 
• It is a significant iron ore-producing region in western India.
 
• It is located along the western coast, spanning parts of Maharashtra and Goa states.
 
• This belt is known for its iron ore deposits, particularly the high-quality hematite ores.
 
 
 
• **The Odisha-Jharkhand belt:-**
 
 
• It is a major iron ore-producing region in eastern India.
 
• It encompasses parts of the states of Odisha and Jharkhand and is one of the richest mineral belts in the country.
 
 
 
• **Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt:**-
 
 
• It is not primarily known as an iron ore-producing region.
 
• Instead, it is a significant geological belt in central India that is rich in mineral resources, including coal and other minerals like limestone, bauxite, and manganese.

questions.question: “World Refugee Day” is observed every year on ______.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **World Refugee Day:-**

 
 
• It is an international observance held annually on June 20th.
 
• It is a day designated by the United Nations to honor the courage, resilience, and strength of millions of refugees worldwide who have been forced to flee their homes due to conflict, persecution, or other forms of violence.
 
• The main purpose of World Refugee Day is to raise awareness about the plight of refugees and to mobilize support for their protection and well-being.
 
• It serves as a reminder that refugees are ordinary people who have been through extraordinary circumstances and deserve compassion, empathy, and assistance.
 
• The theme for World Refugee Day may vary each year, focusing on different aspects of the refugee crisis. It serves as a platform to shed light.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: PARAM 8000, developed in 1991 using parallel processing, belongs to which generation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fifth.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **PARAM:-**

 
 
• **It **is a series of supercomputers developed by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) in India.
 
• It stands for "Parallel Machine." PARAM was one of the earliest supercomputing initiatives in India and has evolved over time to encompass various generations and models.
 
• The PARAM series started with PARAM 8000, which was commissioned in 1991 and was India's first indigenous supercomputer. Since then, several iterations of the PARAM supercomputers have been developed, each offering increased computing power and performance.
 
• Some notable PARAM supercomputers include:
 
 
• PARAM 8000: India's first supercomputer, introduced in 1991.
 
• PARAM 8000 Plus: An upgraded version of PARAM 8000, released in 1994.
 
• PARAM 8600: A supercomputer launched in 1998, which utilized a distributed memory architecture.
 
• PARAM 10000: Introduced in 1998, PARAM 10000 was designed for weather forecasting and other scientific applications.
 
• PARAM Padma: A supercomputer launched in 2002, featuring high computational power and network bandwidth.
 
• PARAM Yuva: A supercomputer unveiled in 2009, offering significant computing capabilities for research and development.
 
• PARAM Shakti: A series of indigenous supercomputers based on RISC-V architecture, developed by C-DAC and announced in 2018. This series aims to promote the development and adoption of the indigenous processor architecture in India.
 
• PARAM Siddhi-AI: An artificial intelligence-focused supercomputer unveiled in 2020, designed to accelerate research in AI and machine learning applications.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to get the Oscar for lifetime achievements in cinema in 1992?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satyajit Ray.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Satyajit Ray:-**

 
 
• Satyajit Ray (1921-1992) was a renowned Indian filmmaker, screenwriter, author, and composer.
 
• He is considered one of the greatest filmmakers in the history of cinema and is often credited with bringing Indian cinema to the global stage.
 
• Ray is particularly known for his realistic and artistic approach to filmmaking, focusing on human relationships and social issues.
 
• Ray's directorial debut came with the film "Pather Panchali" (1955), the first installment of his critically acclaimed Apu Trilogy.
 
 
• The trilogy, which also includes "Aparajito" (1956) and "Apur Sansar" (1959), follows the life of a young boy named Apu and is considered a masterpiece of world cinema.
 
 
 
• Satyajit Ray received numerous awards and accolades throughout his career:-
 
 
• He was honored with the prestigious Legion of Honour by the French government, and in 1992.
 
• He was posthumously awarded the Academy Award for Lifetime Achievement.
 
 
 
 
 
• **The Academy Awards:-**
 
 
• They are also known as the Oscars, are an annual set of awards honoring artistic and technical excellence in the film industry.
 
• The awards are presented by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (AMPAS), and they recognize outstanding achievements in various categories, including acting, directing, writing, and film production.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Tarun Majumdar is an Indian film director and screenwriter known for his work in Bengali cinema.
 
• He was born on February 22, 1931, in Comilla, British India (now Bangladesh).
 
• Majumdar is considered one of the pioneers of the parallel cinema movement in Bengal and is often associated with the "middle cinema" genre.
 
 
 
• **K Viswanath:-**
 
 
• ​Kasinathuni Viswanath, popularly known as K. Viswanath, is an eminent Indian film director, screenwriter, and actor, primarily associated with Telugu cinema.
 
• He was born on February 19, 1930, in Repalle, Andhra Pradesh, India.
 
• Viswanath is known for his artistic and socially relevant films, which have garnered critical acclaim and widespread recognition.
 
 
 
• **T. Rama Rao:-**
 
 
• Nandamuri Taraka Rama Rao (NTR), was a prominent Indian actor, filmmaker, and politician.
 
• He was born on May 28, 1923, in Nimmakuru, Andhra Pradesh, India, and passed away on January 18, 1996.
 
• NTR had a remarkable career in the Telugu film industry, where he acted in over 300 films and gained immense popularity.
 
• He made his acting debut in 1949 with the film "Mana Desam" and went on to portray a wide range of roles, including mythological, historical, and social dramas

questions.question: Which among the following is the correct way to express change of inventories of a firm during a year?

options.text: Change of inventories of a firm during a year (value added – intermediate goods used by the firm + sale of the firm during a year)
Change of inventories of a firm during a year (value added + intermediate goods used by the firm + sale of the firm during a year)
Change of inventories of a firm during a year (value added – intermediate goods used by the firm – sale of the firm during a year)
Change of inventories of a firm during a year (value added + intermediate goods used by the firm – sale of the firm during a year)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Change of inventories of a firm during a year (value added + intermediate goods used by the firm – sale of the firm during a year).**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Point__**

 
• The correct way to express the change of inventories of a firm during a year is by calculating the inventory turnover or by using the formula for the change in inventories.
 
 
• **Inventory Turnover:**

 
 
• Inventory turnover is a financial ratio that measures the number of times a company's inventory is sold and replaced during a given period.
 
• It is calculated by dividing the cost of goods sold (COGS) by the average inventory value.
 
• The formula for inventory turnover is:
 
 
• **Inventory Turnover = Cost of Goods Sold / Average Inventory**
 
 
 
 
 
• **Change in Inventories::-**
 
 
• The change in inventories can be calculated by subtracting the ending inventory value from the beginning inventory value.
 
• The formula for the change in inventories is:
 
 
• **Change in Inventories = Ending Inventory - Beginning Inventory**
 
• This measure represents the net increase or decrease in inventory over a specific period, such as a year. A positive value indicates an increase in inventory, while a negative value suggests a decrease.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of a fold mountain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Rhine Valley**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fold Mountain:-**

 
 
• Fold mountains are a type of mountain formed by the folding of layers of rock in the Earth's crust.
 
• They are characterized by long, linear ridges and valleys that often extend for hundreds of kilometers.
 
• The process of mountain formation through folding is known as orogeny.
 
 
 
• **The Rhine Valley:-**
 
 
• The Rhine Valley refers to the region along the Rhine River, which is one of the major rivers in Europe.
 
• The Rhine River flows through multiple countries, including Switzerland, Germany, France, and the Netherlands.
 
• The Rhine Valley encompasses the areas surrounding the river as it meanders through these countries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Aravali range:-**

 
 
• The Aravali Range is a mountain range located in western India, primarily in the states of Rajasthan and Haryana.
 
• It is one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world, dating back to millions of years.
 
• The Aravali Range stretches approximately 800 kilometers (500 miles) from Gujarat in the southwest to Delhi in the northeast.
 
• It is a type of fold mountain.
 
 
 
• **Appalachians**:-
 
 
• The Appalachians, also known as the Appalachian Mountains or Appalachian Range, are a vast mountain system in eastern North America.
 
• They extend for about 2,400 kilometers (1,500 miles) from Newfoundland and Labrador in Canada, down through the eastern United States, and into northern Alabama in the southeastern part of the country.
 
• The Appalachian Mountains are one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world.
 
• It is a type of fold mountain.
 
 
 
• **Ural Mountains:-**
 
 
• ​It is a mountain range that stretches for about 2,500 kilometers (1,550 miles) from north to south, dividing the European and Asian continents.
 
• The range starts from the Arctic Ocean in the north and extends to the Ural River in the south, which separates Russia into its European and Asian parts.
 
• It is a type of fold mountain.

questions.question: Which of the following countries has decided to opt out of the International Space Station (ISS) after 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Russia.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **International Space Station (ISS):-**

 
 
• **​**The International Space Station (ISS) is a multinational cooperative project involving space agencies from the United States (NASA), Russia (Roscosmos), Europe (ESA), Japan (JAXA), and Canada (CSA).
 
• It is a habitable space station that orbits the Earth and serves as a research laboratory, observatory, and living space for astronauts from different countries.
 
• Russia will opting out of it by the 2024.
 
 
 
• **Roscosmos:-**
 
 
• Roscosmos, also known as the Russian Space Agency, is the government corporation responsible for the space activities of Russia.
 
• It was formed in 1992 following the dissolution of the Soviet Union and the subsequent restructuring of the Russian space industry.
 
• Roscosmos is tasked with various responsibilities related to space exploration, scientific research, and the development of space technologies.
 
• Its primary objectives include the launch and operation of manned and unmanned spacecraft, satellite deployment, and the advancement of space science.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NASA**:-

 
 
• NASA, short for the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, is an independent agency of the United States federal government responsible for the country's civilian space program and for aeronautics and aerospace research.
 
• NASA was established on July 29, 1958, replacing its predecessor, the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics (NACA)
 
 
 
• **JAXA**:-
 
 
• JAXA stands for the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency. It is the national space agency of Japan and is responsible for the country's space exploration, satellite deployment, and aerospace research.
 
• JAXA was formed on October 1, 2003, through the merger of three former organizations: the Institute of Space and Astronautical Science (ISAS), the National Aerospace Laboratory of Japan (NAL), and the National Space Development Agency of Japan (NASDA).

questions.question: Which among the following lakes lies on the borders of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pulicat.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pulicat Lake **(also known as **Pulicat Lagoon**) lies on the borders of **Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.**
 
• Pulicat Lake is the **second-largest brackish water lagoon **in India.
 
• It spans the states of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, with the **majority of its area falling in Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• The lake is separated from the Bay of Bengal by a barrier island known as **Sriharikota.**
 
• Pulicat Lake is home to a **rich variety of flora and fauna**, including numerous **bird species**, making it an important bird sanctuary and an ecologically significant area.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dal Lake:**

 
 
• Dal Lake is a popular tourist attraction located in **Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir.**
 
• It is known for its scenic beauty, serene surroundings, and floating gardens called** "Rad" and "Sankara."**
 
• The lake is surrounded by **snow-capped mountains, Mughal gardens, and charming houseboats.**
 
• **Shikaras,** traditional wooden boats, are commonly used for transportation and sightseeing on Dal Lake.
 
 
 
• **Loktak Lake:**
 
 
• Loktak Lake is the** largest freshwater lake in Northeast India,** situated in **Manipur.**
 
• It is known for its **floating phumdis** (heterogeneous mass of vegetation, soil, and organic matter) that can be seen on the lake's surface.
 
• The lake is home to the **Keibul Lamjao National Park,** which is the **world's only floating national park** and a refuge for the endangered Manipur **brow-antlered deer.**
 
• Loktak Lake plays a crucial role in maintaining the ecological balance and is a significant source of livelihood for the local communities.
 
 
 
• **Sambhar Lake:**
 
 
• Sambhar Lake, located in** Rajasthan**, is the** largest inland saltwater lake in India.**
 
• It is an important wintering area for migratory** birds, including flamingos**, and is recognized as a **Ramsar site.**
 
• Sambhar Lake is known for its **salt production**, and** salt pans **can be seen around the lake's vicinity.
 
• The lake is surrounded by** vast saline wetlands,** giving it a unique landscape and attracting **nature enthusiasts and birdwatchers.**

questions.question: Under ______ (Governor General from 1813 to 1823) a new policy of “paramountcy” was initiated. Now the Company claimed that its authority was paramount or supreme, hence its power was greater than that of Indian states.

questions.question: The nineteenth century saw the golden age of Kathak under the patronage of ____________, the last Nawab of Oudh.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Wajid Ali Shah.

 
• Wajid Ali Shah was the last Nawab of Oudh (Awadh) and reigned from 1847 to 1856.
 
• He was a prominent patron of the arts and played a significant role in the development and promotion of Kathak, a classical dance form of India.
 
• Wajid Ali Shah himself was a skilled dancer, poet, and musician, and he actively supported Kathak performers and musicians during his reign.
 
• Under his patronage, Kathak reached its golden age in the nineteenth century, with the art form flourishing in the royal courts and gaining popularity among the masses.
 
• Asaf-ud-daula:
 
 
• Asaf-ud-daula was the fourth Nawab of Awadh, ruling from 1775 to 1797.
 
• He is known for his patronage of art, architecture, and literature in Lucknow.
 
• Asaf-ud-daula commissioned the construction of several architectural marvels, including the Bara Imambara and the Rumi Darwaza in Lucknow.
 
• He also promoted cultural activities and supported renowned poets and musicians of his time.
 
 
 
• Siraj-ud-daulah:
 
 
• Siraj-ud-daulah was the last independent Nawab of Bengal, reigning from 1756 to 1757.
 
• He is famously associated with the Battle of Plassey in 1757, where he faced defeat against the British East India Company forces led by Robert Clive.
 
• The British victory at Plassey marked a significant turning point in the British colonization of India.
 
• Siraj-ud-daulah's defeat and subsequent capture led to the British gaining control over Bengal and establishing their dominance in the region.
 
 
 
• Saadat Khan Burhanul mulk:
 
 
• Saadat Khan Burhanul mulk, also known as Burhan-ul-Mulk, was a prominent Persian noble and statesman.
 
• He served as the founder of the Nawab dynasty in Awadh and became the first Nawab of Awadh in 1722.
 
• Saadat Khan played a vital role in stabilizing and expanding the Awadh region and was known for his administrative and military reforms.
 
• Under his rule, Awadh witnessed significant development, and he established a well-organized administration and a strong revenue system.

questions.question: The Seventy-First Amendment to the Indian Constitution included Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali languages in the _____ Schedule.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eighth.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** 71st Amendment**, **enacted in 1992,** added **Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali languages** to the** Eighth Schedule** of the Indian Constitution, recognizing them as **official languages of India.**
 
• The amendment was a significant step towards** linguistic inclusivity, acknowledging the cultural and linguistic diversity **of India and granting official status to these languages.
 
• The 71st Amendment highlighted the importance of **preserving and promoting** these languages, ensuring their** protection**, and **facilitating educational resources, official documentation, and communication** in these languages for their respective communities.
 
• The addition of **Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali** languages to the Eighth Schedule aimed to provide representation and support to linguistic communities in **Goa, Manipur, and Sikkim, respectively.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****There are a total of 12 Schedules in the Indian Constitution.**

 
 

 
 
**Schedules**

 
 
 
**Features**

 
 
 

 
 
First Schedule

 
 
 
List of States & Union Territories

 
 
 

 
 
Second Schedule

 
 
 
Salary of President, Governors, Chief Judges, Judges of High Court and Supreme Court, Comptroller and Auditor General.

 
 
 

 
 
Third Schedule

 
 
 
Forms of Oaths and Affirmations

 
 
 

 
 
Fourth Schedule

 
 
 
Allocate seats for each state of India in Rajya Sabha

 
 
 

 
 
Fifth Schedule

 
 
 
Administration and control of scheduled areas and tribes.

 
 
 

 
 
Sixth Schedule

 
 
 
Provisions for the administration of Tribal Areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram 

 
 
 

 
 
Seventh Schedule

 
 
 
Gives allocation of powers and functions between Unions & States. It contains 3 lists Union List, States, Concurrent List

 
 
 

 
 
Eighth Schedule

 
 
 
List of 22 languages of India recognized by the Constitution.

 
 
 

 
 
Ninth Schedule

 
 
 
It contains acts & orders related to land tenure, land tax, railways, and industries.

 
 
 

 
 
Tenth Schedule

 
 
 
It contains provisions for disqualification of grounds of defection.

 
 
 

 
 
Eleventh Schedule

 
 
 
It contains provisions of the Panchayati Raj.

 
 
 

 
 
Twelfth Schedule

 
 
 
It contains provisions of the Municipal Corporation.

questions.question: Buddha meditated for days on end under a peepal tree at ______, where he attained enlightenment.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bodh Gaya.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bodh Gaya** is a small town in the state of **Bihar, India**, and it is **one of the most sacred sites in Buddhism.**
 
• It was at Bodh Gaya, **under a peepal tree** known as the **Bodhi Tree**, that Siddhartha Gautama, later known as Buddha, **attained enlightenment.**
 
• The site of Bodh Gaya is **marked by the Mahabodhi Temple**, which is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site **and an important pilgrimage destination for Buddhists worldwide.
 
• The temple complex houses the** sacred Bodhi Tree,** **the Vajrasana (Diamond Throne)** where Buddha meditated, and various other monastic structures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarnath:**

 
 
• Sarnath, located near** Varanasi **in Uttar Pradesh, is where** Buddha delivered his first sermon **after attaining enlightenment.
 
• It is a significant pilgrimage site for Buddhists.
 
 
 
• **Kushinagar: **
 
 
• Kushinagar, also in Uttar Pradesh, is the place where **Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana (passed away)**.
 
• It is an important Buddhist pilgrimage site and has several **monastic ruins and stupas.**
 
 
 
• **Ujjain: **
 
 
• Ujjain is an ancient city in **Madhya Pradesh **and holds** religious importance in Hinduism.**
 
• It is associated with the** Kumbh Mela **and is known for its ancient temples, but it is not directly linked to Buddha's life or enlightenment.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a type of connective tissue?

I. Blood

II. Bone

III. Ligament
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I, II and III.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Connective tissues** provide** structural support and integrity **to the body, with diverse types such as** loose, dense, adipose, cartilage, bone, and blood,** each contributing unique properties and functions within the extracellular matrix. ***Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.***
 
• The **extracellular matrix,** composed of protein fibres and ground substance, determines the **flexibility, strength, and elasticity of connective tissues,** allowing them to adapt to different mechanical demands.
 
• Apart from their structural roles, connective tissues also play a **crucial role in immunity,** with certain types housing immune cells and contribute to immune responses** against pathogens and foreign substances.**
 
• Connective tissues are essential components of the body, contributing to its **overall architecture, supporting organs and tissues, storing energy, protecting vital structures,** and participating in various **physiological processes.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Blood:**

 
 
• Blood is a type of **connective tissue **that consists of cells suspended in a** liquid matrix called plasma.**
 
• It plays a vital role in** transporting oxygen, nutrients, hormones, and waste products** throughout the body.
 
 
 
• **Bone: **
 
 
• Bone is a specialized** connective tissue** that forms the **skeletal structure of the body.**
 
• It provides **support, protection, and facilitates movement. **
 
• Bone tissue is composed of cells called** osteocytes** embedded in a matrix of **collagen fibres and calcium salts.**
 
 
 
• **Ligament: **
 
 
• Ligaments are **fibrous connective tissues** that connect bones to other bones in a joint.
 
• They provide **stability** and help** limit excessive movement **within the joint, contributing to joint strength and function.

questions.question: Which of the following is an organic impurity in sewage?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Human faeces.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Human faeces are an organic impurity commonly found in sewage.
 
• Faecal matter is rich in organic matter and contains various bacteria, pathogens, and undigested food particles.
 
• The presence of human faeces in sewage poses a risk to public health due to the potential transmission of diseases and contamination of water sources.
 
• Proper sewage treatment processes are necessary to effectively manage and eliminate human faeces to prevent environmental and health hazards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phosphates:**

 
 
• Phosphates are** inorganic compounds** that can be found in sewage as an inorganic impurity.
 
• Phosphates mainly come from** detergents, fertilizers, and human waste** that enter the sewage system.
 
• Excessive levels of phosphates in sewage can contribute to** water pollution and eutrophication** when released into natural water bodies.
 
• **Controlling and reducing the phosphate levels** in sewage is important for environmental protection and maintaining water quality.
 
 
 
• **Nitrates:**
 
 
• Nitrates are inorganic compounds that can be present in sewage as an** inorganic impurity.**
 
• Nitrates can originate from various sources, including **agricultural runoff, industrial waste, and domestic sewage.**
 
• Elevated levels of nitrates in sewage can lead to water pollution and pose a **risk to human health**, especially when they contaminate drinking water sources.
 
 
 
• **Metals:**
 
 
• Metals, such as** lead, mercury, cadmium, and copper, **can be present in sewage as** inorganic impurities.**
 
• These metals can originate from various sources, including** industrial discharges, domestic waste, and runoff from metal-contaminated areas.**
 
• Elevated levels of metals in sewage can have detrimental effects on the environment and human health.
 
• Effective sewage treatment processes, including filtration and sedimentation, are employed to remove or reduce metal impurities in sewage before it is discharged or reused.
